title: Michigan Seller Disclosure Statement
description: Michigan Seller Disclosure Act (MCL 565.951 through 565.966) requires sellers of residential property (1-4 units) to complete a comprehensive Seller's Disclosure Statement before the purchase agreement is signed. The disclosure covers structural conditions, mechanical systems, environmental hazards, zoning, and other material facts.

required_actions.note: Exemptions under MCL 565.956: transfers between co-owners, foreclosures, court-ordered transfers, estate transfers where seller has not occupied property.

title: Agency Disclosure
description: Michigan Occupational Code (MCL 339.2512d) requires licensees to provide a written agency disclosure to all parties at the first substantive contact. Michigan permits buyer agency, seller agency, dual agency (with written consent), and designated agency within the same brokerage.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Michigan follows federal lead paint disclosure requirements under 42 USC §4852d. Additionally, Michigan's Lead Abatement Act (MCL 333.5451 et seq.) provides state-level regulations for lead hazard identification and remediation. Sellers of pre-1978 housing must provide the federal disclosure form and EPA pamphlet.

title: Closing Type — Title Company State
description: Michigan closings are typically handled by title companies or closing agents. An attorney is not required at closing but is recommended. Michigan uses both title insurance and abstracts of title depending on the region of the state.

required_actions.note: Title company or closing agent typically handles settlement. Attorney not required but recommended. Western Michigan often uses abstracts; metro Detroit area uses title insurance.

title: Wetlands and Environmental Disclosure
description: Michigan's seller disclosure form (MCL 565.954) specifically requires disclosure of known wetlands, environmental contamination, and proximity to farms or farm operations. Michigan's Part 303 Wetlands Protection (MCL 324.30301 et seq.) imposes restrictions that affect property use and must be disclosed.

required_actions.note: Included in Michigan Seller's Disclosure Statement. Must disclose known wetlands, environmental contamination, underground storage tanks, and proximity to agricultural operations.
